The pooled gene expression (log2(TPM+1), batch-corrected) distribution across all cell lines is moderately RIGHT-SKEWED (positive skew), with a Fisher–Pearson skewness of ≈ +0.69.

Numbers (pooled over all 1,673 cell lines × 19,138 genes):
- n = 32,017,874 values
- mean = 2.612
- std (population, ddof=0) = 2.505
- skewness (scipy.stats.skew, bias=True) = 0.689708
- skewness (scipy.stats.skew, bias=False) = 0.689708 (practically identical given the very large n)
- range: min = -2.623, max = 18.437

Characterisation: The distribution has a long upper tail (right/positive skew, ~0.69), consistent with log2(TPM+1) expression data where a small number of highly expressed gene-cells push the tail to the right while the bulk of values cluster near the mean (~2.6). The skewness describes the supplied batch-corrected values, not raw TPM; batch correction is also why a few values fall slightly below zero.

payload.shape: moderately right-skewed (positive skew, long upper tail)
